ca_hemingway_buttress_e_face_mid.blurb: The middle stretch of the long east-facing wall at Hemingway Buttress, in the Lost Horse part of Joshua Tree National Park at roughly 4,200 feet. It is a trad-focused wall of a dozen routes, nearly all on gear with a single top-rope line, and the grades start around 5.8 and climb to the low 5.11s. The bulk of the lines sit between 5.9 and 5.11, so it suits climbers who already lead moderate to hard cracks and faces. The walk from the lot is short, about ten minutes on a signed path.
